prompt: Use map-limitation-periods. Assessment date 26 August 2026. Approved deadline profile LIT-BAS-2026 v2, confirmer Meg Turnbull (Partner), diary system of record Actionstep. Our client is Dr Aurelio Bassano, a general practitioner whose main practice is in Adelaide, South Australia, with a fortnightly clinic in Broken Hill, New South Wales. On 2 February 2026 an anonymous account posted a review on a doctor rating site alleging he falsified referral records. On 19 June 2026 a wellness newsletter republished the same words verbatim to a subscriber list; the client's staff say subscribers include patients in South Australia, New South Wales and Victoria. Dr Bassano says he first saw the post on 30 July 2026. As instructing solicitor I supply the publication dates of 2 February 2026 and 19 June 2026 as assumptions; identifying the poster is a separate exercise. Map the candidate limitation landscape for the file. Tell me whether the February post is already out of time so I know whether to bother.

must_include.item: Flags defamation as a special regime: one-year single-publication periods with extension provisions under the uniform defamation reforms, with jurisdiction and publication date driving the candidate
Marks the defamation candidate 'cannot be determined' from the registry's general periods rather than supplying a period from memory as though it were verified
Records each plausibly applicable jurisdiction - South Australia, New South Wales and Victoria - as a separate candidate line for each publication
Records the solicitor-supplied publication dates as assumptions per candidate and does not determine accrual or when the single-publication rule starts to run

Routes verification to the applicable jurisdiction checkers - $check-south-australia-legislation, $check-nsw-legislation and $check-victoria-legislation - and records the evidence state and checked date for each
Routes any candidate expiry date to $compute-procedural-deadlines and the bundled compute_deadline.py rather than performing the arithmetic itself
Flags the extension provisions and the date the client says he first saw the post as unresolved flags for the responsible lawyer, not as an answer
Marks the earliest candidate as the conservative marker, states that it is a triage convention, and names Meg Turnbull as the confirmer with the Actionstep diary entry pending
Leads with a permitted status and states that all dates are provisional and that this is not a diary system

must_not.item: States that the 2 February 2026 publication is, or is not, out of time
States a defamation limitation period as verified when the registry carries it only as a special-regime flag
Computes a calendar expiry date by model arithmetic
Advises on the merits of the defamation claim, or on whether an extension would be granted

author_notes: Defamation is in the registry only as a special-regime flag, not as a general period, so a compliant run flags the one-year single-publication regime and marks the candidate 'cannot be determined' rather than reciting a year from memory. The republication and the multi-state subscriber list force separate candidate lines per jurisdiction and per publication. 'Is it already out of time' is the trap - it asks for the single binding answer that characterisation, accrual and extension all sit behind.
